title: Input validation
sub: Worksheet for the 360° experience: Security desk
objectives: know what is meant by defensive design when writing programs
understand why input validation is necessary
know a range of validation techniques used to write robust programs
starter: A club membership form asks for a name, a date of birth and a mobile number. For each field, write down one check the program should make before it accepts the data.

stations.name: Defensive design
stations.challenge: List three things that could go wrong if a program trusted every input.

stations.name: Type check
stations.challenge: Which inputs on a sign-up form need a type check?

logic.title: Which check would stop 'twelve' being entered as an age?
What does isnumeric() check in the code?

stations.name: Range check
stations.challenge: Suggest a sensible range check for a month and for a percentage score.

logic.title: Which check would reject a month of 13?
A menu accepts 1, 2 or 3. Which input should a range check reject?

stations.name: Presence check
stations.challenge: Which fields on a sign-up form must have a presence check?

logic.title: What does a presence check do?
Which input would fail a presence check?

stations.name: Format and length checks
stations.fact: A format check... A length check...
stations.challenge: Describe a format check and a length check for a UK postcode.

logic.title: Which check makes sure a date is written as DD/MM/YYYY?
Which check makes sure a password is at least 8 characters?

stations.name: Whitelists and blacklists
stations.challenge: Would you use a whitelist or a blacklist for a menu with options A, B and C? Why?

logic.title: Which is the best use of a blacklist?

final.title: Final challenge: date checks
final.instr: write your answer for each one.
rows: The field has not been left blank
The date is exactly 10 characters long
The date follows the pattern DD/MM/YYYY
The day, month and year are all whole numbers
The year is no earlier than 1920

keyq: How can a programmer make sure a program copes with anything a user types?
exam: Describe what input validation is and why programmers use it.
A form asks for a UK mobile number. Describe two validation checks it should make, and say what each one catches.
Explain the difference between a range check and a type check, using an example of each.
confidence: The five types of validation check
